item.title: Syria conflict: 'Cautious calm' returns to Sweida; Druze-Bedouin fighting killed over 1,100
item.description: A fragile calm has settled over Sweida, Southern Syria, after a week of intense sectarian violence that claimed over 1,100 lives. A ceasefire, brokered after multiple failed attempts, is holding between Druze factions and Sunni Bedouin rivals. Government forces have secured parts of the province, and humanitarian aid has begun to arrive.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US faces first megafire risk of 2025: Oregon wildfire burns over 95,000 acres; more than 900 firefighters work on containment
item.description: Oregon's Cram Fire, the largest US wildfire this year, has consumed over 95,740 acres, with 49% containment achieved. Over 900 emergency personnel are battling the blaze, which destroyed homes and triggered evacuations. Favorable weather is aiding efforts, but the fire would become a megafire if it reaches the 100,000 acres mark.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Japan politics: PM Ishiba's coalition loses upper house majority; first time loss for LDP in both chambers since 1955
item.description: Japan's ruling coalition, led by Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba, lost its majority in the upper house, intensifying political uncertainty amid economic woes and rising populism. Voters expressed frustration over stagnant wages, soaring prices, and stricter immigration policies. The defeat weakens Ishiba's position, potentially leading to internal challenges and complicating trade talks with the U.S.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Netanyahu falls ill: Israeli PM suffering from food poisoning; will work from home for 3 days
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is currently resting at his residence after being diagnosed with food poisoning, his office confirmed. Doctors have treated the 75-year-old leader for intestinal inflammation and dehydration. Consequently, his ongoing corruption trial has been postponed, with the next hearing scheduled for September.

item.title: This K-Pop band is making waves with sign language
item.description: Big Ocean, a unique K-pop group with deaf or hard-of-hearing members, is captivating global audiences. Using innovative audio technology and Korean Sign Language, Lee Chan-yeon, Park Hyun-jin, and Kim Ji-seok have achieved remarkable success. Following their debut with "Glow," they've garnered international recognition, including Billboard's Rookie of the Month and Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni

item.title: Border agent shot in NYC park: Suspect had deportation order; Trump blames Biden policy
item.description: An off-duty US Border Patrol agent was shot in the face during a robbery in a New York City park. The suspect, Miguel Francisco Mora Nunez, an illegal immigrant with a prior deportation order, was apprehended. The agent returned fire, wounding Mora, who has a history of arrests and was previously released due to overcrowding despite his immigration status.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kristin Cabot caught in viral video: CEO quits, wife reacts; scandal rocks Boston elite
item.description: Kristin Cabot, Astronomer's HR executive, is at the center of a scandal after a video of her cuddling CEO Andy Byron went viral, leading to his resignation and social media fallout. Cabot is reportedly married into the wealthy Cabot family of Boston, known for their historical prominence and roots in the carbon black industry.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bangladesh set to revive caretaker govt system
item.description: Bangladeshi political stakeholders have agreed to reinstate the caretaker government system, abolished over a decade ago, following 14 years of struggle. The agreement was reached during discussions initiated by the National Consensus Commission. However, Awami League and Jatiya Party did not participate in the Muhammad Yunus-headed interim government's political dialogue.

item.title: Close call: Delta Airlines flight makes ‘aggressive maneuver’ mid-air to avoid B-52 bomber; ‘not a fun day at work’ says pilot
item.description: A Delta regional jet, SkyWest flight 3788, narrowly avoided a mid-air collision with a B-52 bomber near Minot, North Dakota, on July 18. The pilot took evasive action after spotting the bomber, citing a lack of prior warning from air traffic control despite the nearby Minot Air Force Base having radar capabilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘They’ll do it again’: Slain US intern’s mother warns after DC shooting; FBI offers $40K reward
item.description: The mother of Eric Tarpinian-Jachym, a congressional intern fatally shot in Washington, D.C., is demanding justice and warning other parents. The 21-year-old UMass Amherst student was unintentionally caught in targeted gunfire. Authorities are offering a $40,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the shooters, as the FBI assists local police in the investigation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Keep spreading the word’: Tommy Robinson shares cryptic message on social media; urges people to assemble in London
item.description: Far-right British activist Tommy Robinson has called for supporters to gather in London on September 13th, sparking significant interest, particularly from Ireland. The purpose of the assembly remains undisclosed. Robinson, known for his controversial views and past convictions, enjoys a strong online following, including support from Elon Musk, who has defended him as a truth-teller suppressed by the state.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Profoundly grateful’: Number of missing in deadly Texas floods drops from nearly 100 to 3; search operations to continue
item.description: Following devastating Texas floods, the number of missing in Kerr County has drastically reduced from nearly 100 to just 3, with most located safe. Kerrville City Manager Dalton Rice expressed gratitude for the tireless efforts of over 1,000 authorities. The floods, exceeding a 100-year event, claimed numerous lives, especially in Kerr County where the Guadalupe River surged rapidly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Highest ever’ numbers: Trump claims support from MAGA base gone up ‘significantly’; pressure from ‘troublemakers’ over Epstein files persist
item.description: Donald Trump claims his poll numbers within the Republican Party have surged amid the Jeffrey Epstein controversy, citing figures as high as 95%. This comes as Trump faces scrutiny over his past association with Epstein, including the release of a note mentioning his name. He has denied writing the note and filed a defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal.

item.title: UAE: Air Arabia wins bid to launch Saudi low-cost airline in Dammam, boosting Vision 2030 goals
item.description: UAE-based Air Arabia, in partnership with Saudi firms Kun Investment Holding and Nesma Group, has won the bid to launch a new Saudi low-cost airline based in Dammam. With a planned fleet of 45 aircraft, the airline aims to serve 81 destinations and support Vision 2030 by boosting regional connectivity, competition, and access across Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Turkey's Erdogan insists on Cyprus two-state solution
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Sunday reaffirmed his country's support for a two-state solution in Cyprus, urging the international community to accept the Mediterranean island's existing division. "We fully support the vision based on a two-state solution," Erdogan said during a visit to northern Cyprus marking 51 years since Turkish troops invaded the island.

item.title: 18-hour days, 1 week off: UAE Prime Minister's relentless commitment to nation and people
item.description: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed leads by staying close to the people. Despite a demanding schedule, he takes time to connect personally with students, athletes, workers, and foster mothers. His leadership is marked by humility and genuine presence, showing that real leadership means listening and being part of the community, not just holding a title.

item.title: Dubai car leasing in 2025: Costs, rules and best options for expats
item.description: In 2025, Dubai offers appealing car leasing options, especially for expats seeking flexibility and lower costs. Leasing provides access to new models with maintenance and insurance included, avoiding hefty down payments. Options range from traditional leases to lease-to-own plans, with economy cars starting around AED 1,200 monthly. A UAE driving license, Emirates ID, and proof of income are required.
